task.description: Hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's design at lib/letflow/design/req372-semantic-decision-rule-validation.md, per WF-02 Step 1b (docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md) and .claude/agents/code-design-validator.md. You are on branch feature/WF02-REQ372-20260921 -- verify with git branch --show-current first. Read the design artefact directly (not CODE-DESIGNER's handoff result.summary as a substitute). For each of the 10 acceptance criteria listed in this handoff's task.acceptance_criteria: does the design have a corresponding concrete design element, with no TBD/deferral language? Are function signatures fully specified (name, inputs, outputs, error cases, @spec-style)? Is the error/success shape stated (tagged tuples, not left implicit)? Are cross-module dependencies listed? Is there NO implementation code present (no .ex code bodies -- signatures and type shapes only)? Specifically scrutinize these load-bearing decisions the designer made, since they are exactly the kind of thing this gate exists to catch if under-justified: (a) the release/promotion submission call path identified (which function(s) exactly, and is the justification for that choice -- reading promotion.ex and definitions.ex -- actually sound, not just asserted); (b) the comparable/non-comparable type-pair table (is it complete, unambiguous, and does it correctly mark numeric/money vs text/string as non-comparable per the acceptance criteria's explicit minimum); (c) the HUMAN_TASK-out-of-scope decision (is the reasoning genuinely grounded in a real grep/read of the code, not just asserted); (d) confirm the design proposes ZERO changes to lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex's grammar/parser (a pure read-only consumer of its already-parsed AST) -- REQ-288's EXP-102 decision must stand unmodified; (e) confirm the design's chosen call-site change for create/2 and update/2 (the designer reportedly left these UNCHANGED, wiring the new pass only into activate/2 and validate_definition_graph/2) is explicitly justified against the requirement's own acceptance criteria, not silently narrower than what the criteria demand -- this is exactly the kind of divergence-from-precedent a design gate must catch, not wave through. FAIL immediately on any check failure -- no partial credit, name every failed check by acceptance criterion or design-quality dimension.
acceptance_criteria: a definition whose EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edge condition references a variable name absent from the definition's declared VariableSchema fields produces a violation naming the exact typed variable name and the step/edge it belongs to, proven by a test

that violation's message includes a suggested nearest declared field name, computed by a real string-distance measure (not a placeholder or first-alphabetical fallback), proven by a test with a clear one-typo case (e.g. 'cusotmer_name' when 'customer_name' is declared)

a definition comparing two operands of declared VariableSchema types this requirement records as non-comparable (at minimum: a numeric/money type against a text/string type) produces a violation, proven by a test; the comparable/non-comparable type-pair table is stated explicitly in the moduledoc, not left implicit

a definition with two independent broken rules (one field-existence violation, one type-compatibility violation) produces BOTH violations in a single validation call, proven by a test -- the author is never required to fix one to discover the other
a definition with zero semantic violations validates cleanly, proven by a test, including after both of the above violations are corrected in the same test

the semantic validation pass re-runs in full (not from a cached prior result) at the definition's actual release/promotion submission call path, proven by a test that changes the underlying VariableSchema or expression state between an earlier clean validation and the submission call, and asserts the submission call reflects the fresh state

whether a HUMAN_TASK routing/assignment-by-field mechanism is in scope for this requirement is stated explicitly in the moduledoc with the reasoning, not left for a reader to infer from what tests do or don't cover
git diff shows lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex unmodified, or if modified, modified only in ways that add no token/operator/builtin -- state which, per REQ-288's precedent
no file under web/ is modified by this requirement
mix letflow.check passes, with real output quoted

result.summary: Independently verified (direct source reads, not CODE-DESIGNER's summary) every one of the five specifically-named scrutiny points and they all hold up: (a) the release/promotion call-path finding is correct -- confirmed by reading promotion.ex in full (no `Graph.` call anywhere, `create_changeset/2` copy-verbatim path) and definitions.ex (activate/2 -> run_activate_transaction/4 -> run_service_scope_validator/3 at lines 2280-2319 calls no Graph validator today, matching line numbers exactly); (b) the comparable/non-comparable type-pair table is complete, unambiguous, and correctly marks numeric vs string as VIOLATION, matching Letflow.EventStore.Registry.JsonSchema.matches_type?/2's real 7-value type vocabulary (string/number/integer/boolean/object/array/null) verified in lib/letflow/event_store/registry/json_schema.ex:82-93, including the 'format is permitted and inert' claim which is a verbatim-sourced phrase from that same file's moduledoc (not json_schema_shape.ex as the citation context could suggest, but correctly the Registry.JsonSchema module the sentence names); (c) the HUMAN_TASK-out-of-scope reasoning is genuinely grounded -- verified check_human_task_role/1 (graph.ex:760-771) requires only a non-blank plain string, and grepped all 5 files referencing Expr. under lib/letflow/ (transition.ex, graph.ex, form_schema_expressions.ex, form_expression_reevaluation.ex, entities/query/types.ex) -- none routes a HUMAN_TASK attribute through Expr; (d) confirmed zero diff to lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex on this branch (git diff --stat main...HEAD is empty for that path), and the design calls only two already-public functions (translate_cel_to_expr/1, parse_strict/1, confirmed public at expr.ex:211/550) with no grammar/token/operator/builtin addition proposed; (e) the create/2 and update/2 exclusion is explicitly and non-silently justified against the requirement's own UAT-scenario acceptance language (EO-001/EO-002, cited directly) rather than left as an unexplained narrowing, and is separately flagged for REVIEWER as a real behavioral divergence from REQ-288's precedent -- this is exactly the transparent-tradeoff shape the gate wants, not a silent gap. All 10 ACs map to a concrete, unambiguous design element; no TBD/deferral language found anywhere in the file (grepped). However, the design fails the gate's own mechanical, no-partial-credit rule against 'no implementation code -- signatures and type shapes only, not bodies' (WF-02 Step 1b check (e); .claude/agents/code-design-validator.md's 'no real .ex/.exs bodies'): section 3.2 and 3.3 contain complete, literal, copy-pasteable Elixir function bodies, not signatures.
issues: Design-quality dimension 'no implementation code present' (WF-02 Step 1b check 2e): section 3.3's `validate_definition_graph/2` is reproduced as a COMPLETE function body -- full `with` clause, full violations concatenation including the new `SemanticValidation.validate/2` call, full return tuple -- with no ellipsis and no 'described, not written' caveat (contrast with section 3.2's own `run_semantic_validation/2', which the doc explicitly labels 'Body (described, not written)'). This is implementation code, not a signature.

Design-quality dimension 'no implementation code present' (WF-02 Step 1b check 2e): section 3.2's call-site code block (the `%ProcessDefinition{status: :draft} = definition -> case ... end` snippet) is a complete, literal replacement for the current lines 2296-2300 of definitions.ex, not a signature or type shape -- it is implementation-ready control flow.

Design-quality dimension 'no implementation code present' (WF-02 Step 1b check 2e): section 3.2's two new `interpret_activate_result/1` private function clauses are given complete literal bodies (`do: error` for both), not signatures -- e.g. `defp interpret_activate_result({:error, {:semantic_validation_failed, _violations}} = error), do: error`.
